newsitem.title: USA: US Airways to start layoffs June 30 - Post.
newsitem.headline: US Airways to start layoffs June 30 - Post.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc.'s board of directors will begin laying off pilots and other employees June 30 unless a last-minute agreement is reached with employees on cutting costs, a newspaper reported Sunday.
The Washington Post quoted company sources as saying the layoffs would begin the day the pilot union's no-layoff clause expires.
The airline last week said it returned to profitability in the first quarter, but added that it suffered losses in key markets and needed to cut costs to remain competitive.

The company has been struggling to reach a labor agreement with its pilots and has raised the possibility that it could reduce the size of the airline to remain competitive if no agreement is reached.

The sources told the Post the final deadline would be Sept. 30 when US Airways must affirm or cancel a $14 billion order for up to 400 new aircraft from Airbus Industrie, the European airline consortium.

The company's chairman, Stephen Wolf, recently appealed to airline employees at a meeting, the newspaper said, telling them that time was running out to agree to concessions. Without agreement on cutting costs, he told employees he would be forced to downsize the airline.
Asked by a pilot in the audience how quickly the end could come, Wolf replied, "I don't know, but clearly sometime in the not-too-distant future."
The meeting was one of a series of meetings with airline employees around the country.

The key issue in the airline's talks with the pilots is just how much of the airline's future operations will be run as a low-cost, low-fare carrier with lower pay and far fewer work rules for its pilots, the newspaper quoted company sources as saying.
